content.title: About
content.content: A cheese muffin is a soft baked good made from wheat flour, eggs, milk, and grated cheese. It has a gentle aroma, a slightly sweet dough flavor, and a pronounced cheesy note. Suitable for breakfast or a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheese muffins are popular in the US and the UK, often served in cafés.
There are many variations: cheddar, mozzarella, parmesan, and even blue cheese.
The batter usually does not require a long rise, so muffins bake quickly.
Cheese in the batter increases protein content and gives a golden crust.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cheese provides a good source of complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium from cheese supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential (when using fermented cheeses)
items.content: Some cheeses, like camembert, may contribute to a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or casein allergy may react to cheese muffins.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Cheese muffins are high in fat and calories, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheese is often salty, which can be an issue for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheese muffins can be enjoyed warm straight from the oven or reheated in a microwave. They pair well with salads, soups, or as part of a brunch spread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days or in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Reheat to 180 °C before serving to restore a crisp crust.
